title: How Going Over Niagara Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore how and why people go over Niagara Falls, covering the geography and size of the three falls (Horseshoe, American, Bridal Veil), their erosion history and Goat Island's name, and the stunt history of daredevils who went over in barrels and other craft. Notable cases include Annie Edson Taylor (first, 1901, with her cat), Bobby Leach, Charles Stevens, George Stathakis with his turtle Sunny Boy, Nathan Boya (first African American, fined in 1961), Kirk Jones (2003, survived after jumping in with no flotation), Peter DeBernardi and Jeffrey Petkevich (anti-drug barrel stunt), and Jesse Sharpe. They also discuss research on daredevil personality (testosterone, serotonin, and a mouse study on the Stanley gene). The episode ends with a listener mail segment of hiku poems and a sponsor read.
topics: going over Niagara Falls in a barrel

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about a finger game and a listener mind-melt challenge, then introduce Niagara Falls and the people who go over it in barrels.

segments.title: Niagara Falls geography and erosion
segments.summary: The hosts describe the three sets of falls (Horseshoe, American, Bridal Veil), the falls eroding backward a few feet a year, the islands that split the river, and the origin of the name Goat Island.

segments.title: Falls statistics
segments.summary: Chuck gives statistics on the drop heights and water flow rates of Horseshoe and American Falls and notes why people choose Horseshoe Falls.

segments.title: Daredevil psychology
segments.summary: The hosts discuss research suggesting daredevils have higher testosterone and lower serotonin, and a mouse study on the Stanley gene and fear memory.

segments.title: Annie Edson Taylor and Bobby Leach
segments.summary: Annie Edson Taylor went over in a pickle barrel with a cat in 1901 and died penniless. Bobby Leach went over in a steel barrel in 1911, was badly injured, and later died after slipping on an orange peel.

segments.title: Charles Stevens and George Stathakis
segments.summary: Charles Stevens died in an oak barrel with an anvil ballast and his feet strapped down. George Stathakis went over with his pet turtle Sunny Boy in 1930 and was trapped behind the water curtain; he likely suffocated, but the turtle survived.

segments.title: Nathan Boya and the 1961 fine
segments.summary: Nathan Boya, the first African American to go over the falls, survived in a metal sphere with a breathing apparatus in 1961 and became the first person fined for the illegal stunt.

segments.title: Kirk Jones and the 2003 jump
segments.summary: Kirk Jones jumped in with no flotation in 2003 after being contemplating suicide, went over Horseshoe Falls, and survived; he described the experience.

segments.title: DeBernardi and Petkevich, other deaths
segments.summary: Peter DeBernardi and Jeffrey Petkevich went over in a barrel in the late 1980s as an anti-drug statement. The hosts also mention a jet ski stunt that ended in death and Jesse Sharpe, who died in a kayak without safety gear.

segments.title: Hiku theater listener mail
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read listener hiku poems and announce a T-shirt winner, Timothy Sinclair, and mention Eric Jones's Appalachian Trail hike.

segments.title: Sponsor read and sign-off
segments.summary: A brief sponsor reference and closing remarks direct listeners to the show's email address.
